title: EDUcore Enhanced Cockburn Use Case Standard v0.11 -- Case Document
description: The machine-readable form of the v0.11 standard: the JSON Schema for a single authored use-case document. This file is NORMATIVE -- where it and the specification prose disagree, this file governs. The specification transcludes it; it is not a copy of the specification. A scenario item must carry a story, an invokes, or both -- the `anyOf` below states that rule at the document layer. Rules that need the assembled graph rather than one document live in v011-shapes.ttl.

nodeRef.description: Reference to a shared node by identifier. Deliberately its own definition: every typed inline definition below is disjoint from it by construction, so a value can never satisfy two oneOf branches -- the trap documented in the userStory and subject repairs. Most typed definitions admit no `ref` key at all; subjectCitation admits one but requires `kind` and `role`, which this closed form excludes, so disjointness holds there too (and nodeRef never shares a oneOf with subjectCitation).

elementCitation.$comment: Identifier syntax is governed by resolutionRegistry.json -- the registry is the identifier-syntax authority (an identifier is the target's stableId or a registry-declared shorthand); Layer 4 executes resolution. Two rules are enforced HERE so the contract has teeth before the resolver exists: the CEDS shorthand conditional, and linked-implies-registry-standard. The registry-key enum below MUST exactly equal resolutionRegistry.json's key set; cases/testIdentityContract.py asserts the sync mechanically. The schema is version-free by ruling (ratification Q7): no standardVersion, anywhere.

identifier.description: EVERY corpus-internal namespace is banned here (Wave 2 closed the worlds leak: a fresh `event:`/`cond:` identifier used to pass as a fake orphan and SATISFY grounding): a Subject is cited with kind `subject`, an intermediate with kind `intermediate` -- never as an element (the identity pun the resolution contract kills). The banned alternation is the namespacePrefix enum minus `orphan:` (cases/testReferenceIntegrity.py asserts the derivation mechanically); `orphan:` identifiers remain legal: a confirmed standards gap is an element-to-be.

allOf.$comment: CEDS shorthand rule (ratification: CEDS-only shorthand at first; duplication with the registry accepted for CEDS alone so the contract bites before the Phase-3 resolver exists). P-prefix = property, C-prefix = class; bare six digits and 'CEDS ######' space forms are ILLEGAL.
Linked implies a NAMED, REGISTERED standard (decision 2.3 + adjudicated decision 1): a citation claiming linkage must name a registry key. Orphan and proposed citations may carry standard null.

standardCitation.$comment: The standard field is an enum of registry keys -- it MUST exactly equal resolutionRegistry.json's key set (cases/testIdentityContract.py asserts the sync mechanically). Prose names ('W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0', 'IMS OpenBadge v3p0 (...)') are not registry keys and do not conform. The schema is version-free by ruling (ratification Q7).

subjectCitation.description: A corpus-internal citation of some case's Subject (or a declared constituent). A subject citation REFERENCES, never defines -- the definition lives where it always has, in a case's subject slot; `ref` must resolve there (checked at the corpus layer, not in this document schema). Deliberately admits NO linkageStatus and NO standard: subjects are corpus-internal by construction, and those fields would be lies waiting to happen. Subject citations do not satisfy the data-grounding invariant.

intermediateCitation.description: A case's own working data: produced things that are neither standards elements nor any case's Subject. Namespace `intermediate:` -- the full word, deliberately identical to the kind name (ratified 2026-07-29; the spelling `int:` is REJECTED). Defined by first use within the owning case, referenced by identifier thereafter; dedup scope is the corpus. Admits NO linkageStatus and NO standard. Intermediate citations do not satisfy the data-grounding invariant.

namespacePrefix.description: The complete enumeration of legal namespace prefixes for corpus identifiers, recorded from the corpus census of 2026-07-29. `vd:`, `ip:`, and `artifact:` are included because the corpus genuinely uses them; `art:` was removed 2026-07-29 when Phase 2 normalized its two sites to `artifact:` (the full-word precedent).
namespacePrefix.$comment: RATIFIED 2026-07-29 (governance Q5): namespaces are an enumeration in the ratified schema, changed only by or at the behest of the coalition. Changing this enum is a coalition act post-ratification. Identifiers within a namespace are registered first-come at the editing tool under AI guidance: authors own names; the commons owns the naming system.

corpusIdentifier.description: Any corpus-internal identifier: one of the ratified namespace prefixes followed by the generic identifier body (qualifier suffixes legal in every namespace; today only subj: and artifact: use them -- recorded, not restricted). The alternation in this pattern MUST mechanically equal the namespacePrefix enum -- cases/testReferenceIntegrity.py asserts the sync (GS-namespaceEnumSync).

dataCitation.description: Any citation kind: element, standard-wholesale, or artifact.

producibleCitation.description: PRODUCES targets DataElement | Standard | OrphanElement -- never SourceArtifact (v011-spec.md, *The grounding*: CONSUMES admits artifacts, PRODUCES does not; artifacts are read-only inputs).

governableCitation.description: GOVERNS targets DataElement only (v011-spec.md: `UseCase -[GOVERNS]-> DataElement`, `Subject -[GOVERNS]-> DataElement`). An element citation whose linkageStatus is not `orphan` -- an orphan projects as OrphanElement, which GOVERNS may not target.

event.description: An Event, typed inline. Through the first v0.11 build an inline event was matched by an untyped inline branch, so {"banana": 12} was a conforming trigger.

condition.description: A Condition, typed inline: a checkable claim.

scopeObject.description: Scope in its object form: an identifiable, reusable boundary entity.

userStory.description: A behavioral unit: what someone does, why, and the data it touches. Typed so that an inline story is VALIDATED rather than merely tolerated.

consumes.description: External citations (element / standard-wholesale / artifact) plus the corpus-internal kinds `subject` and `intermediate`. Branches are disjoint by `kind` const.

produces.description: Producible external citations (element / standard-wholesale -- never artifact) plus the corpus-internal kinds `subject` and `intermediate`. A step that produces a subject citation produces the very node that is some case's Subject.

serves.description: ValueDrivers this unit serves (SERVES). Every target must also appear in the case's valueDrivers[].

$explanation.description: Editorial provenance: what this case was ported from, which source issue it answers, and what changed in the porting. Read by nothing; no invariant depends on it. Named with a leading $ to mark it as ABOUT the document rather than part of the case.

orderingAsserted.description: When true, the case's dependency DAG (declared dependsOn UNION derived data-flow) is a deliberate and COMPLETE claim: the absence of an edge asserts independence, and consumers may parallelize accordingly. When absent or false, the ordering is unanalyzed: the absence of an edge asserts nothing, and consumers MUST treat the numbering as a presumed total order. Silence is the weakest claim, not the strongest.

dependsOn.description: codedNotations of steps in THIS case that must complete before this step, for control prerequisites not already implied by data-flow. Absent = data-flow-only (prerequisites are just the producers of the data this step consumes); [] is equivalent to absent.

invokes.description: id of the UseCase this step invokes -- a bare UseCase id, as in relatedUseCases. A step must have a story, an invokes, or both.

notes.description: ALIGNS_WITH edge property: why THIS case serves the driver.

guarantees.description: At least one guarantee, and at least one of role 'success'. A case must state what success IS, not only what starts it.

comprises.description: External kinds ONLY, forever (ratified Q3): a Subject comprises material from the shared world. The corpus-internal kinds `subject` and `intermediate` are deliberately refused here.

governs.description: External kinds ONLY, forever (ratified Q3): GOVERNS targets shared-world DataElements; the corpus-internal kinds `subject` and `intermediate` are deliberately refused here.
Case-level GOVERNS: methodology grounding when no Subject carries it.

sourceDataRequired.description: External kinds ONLY, forever (ratified Q3): a case's required source data is what it needs from the shared world -- elements, standards, artifacts. The corpus-internal kinds `subject` and `intermediate` are deliberately refused here; a case does not ground by naming its own laundry.
